description:
🚀 MissionMint is a creative space-mission design game built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Players design spacecraft, choose scientific instruments, manage resources such as mass, power, budget, and communications, and make decisions that affect mission success.

MissionMint combines space science, game development, AI, interactive visualization, and storytelling to make space-mission engineering fun and easy to explore.

🌙 Design the mission. 🛰️ Make the decisions. 🚀 Explore beyond.
summary: ODYSSEUS is a 2D space mission design and flight operations game built around a connected four-mission story. Players choose science payloads, weigh mass, power and data trade-offs, then pilot Pathfinder through navigation gates and a controlled docking approach. Mission Control tracks fuel, power, crew reserves, communications, temperature, radiation and science return. Each completed flight advances the mystery and unlocks the next operation. The game makes systems engineering tangible by showing how design choices affect mission performance and crew safety. Its physics and telemetry are simplified for learning; all in-game values are simulated. The current campaign is single-player.
details:
ODYSSEUS is a 2D mission-design and flight-operations game created in Unity 6 for Windows PC. Players select a scientific payload and review its effect on spacecraft mass, power demand, data volume, and mission score. In flight, they guide Pathfinder through navigation gates, manage relative speed, and attempt a controlled docking approach. Mission Control displays simulated mission phase, fuel, electrical power, oxygen, water, food, communications, bus temperature, radiation, crew condition, elapsed time, and science return.

The four-flight campaign connects each objective into one mystery: Mission 002, Orbital Rendezvous, recovers Ariadne Station’s damaged navigation core; Mission 003, Solar Array Service, repairs the Helios array and traces an anomalous signal; Mission 004, The Unscheduled Burn, intercepts a drifting relay and retrieves its future-dated course record; Mission 005, Shadow Window, captures a signal during a short eclipse window and resolves the story. Successful docking advances the campaign, and completion records persist locally. Debriefs explain how payload and piloting choices affect science return and crew safety.

The project is an educational prototype, not a high-fidelity astrodynamics simulator. Telemetry and resource rates are simulated; no NASA datasets, APIs, or real spacecraft telemetry are used. The campaign is single-player; the lobby does not synchronize shared mission state. Generative image tools were used to create original game art, and AI assistance supported code and copy drafting. These contributions are identified in the project documentation and demo. ODYSSEUS was implemented in Unity and C#.
